claim: Azure Data Studio retired 28 February 2026; VS Code + MSSQL extension is the replacement, but SQL Server Agent and full administration remain in Windows-only SSMS.
quote: Azure Data Studio is retired as of February 28, 2026 and no longer receives updates or security fixes... Keep job scheduling and classic administration tasks in SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), which remains the supported home for SQL Server Agent and general administration.

claim: SQL Server containers are supported on Linux hosts with Intel/AMD x86-64 CPUs; emulation layers are not supported.
quote: SQL Server container images are supported only on Linux hosts running on Intel and AMD x86-64 CPUs. Emulation or translation environments (for example, Rosetta 2, Prism, or QEMU) aren't tested or supported.

claim: Microsoft 365 desktop apps are supported only on Windows and macOS; the web version in a browser is the supported route on Linux.
quote: Microsoft 365 desktop applications such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint are officially supported on Windows and macOS only.

claim: Office for the web lacks VBA, third-party add-ins and offline use, and degrades on large or complex files.
quote: Microsoft 365 for the web provides basic editing and viewing features, but it does not have the full feature set of the desktop Office programs.

claim: Thunderbird 145 adds native Exchange over EWS with OAuth2 for M365, but calendar, contacts and Microsoft Graph are not implemented.
quote: Not yet implemented - calendar syncing is on the roadmap... Not yet implemented - Microsoft Graph integration will be added in the future.

claim: Rider runs on Linux and covers .NET development, but has no visual designers for WPF or WinForms.
quote: Rider runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

claim: The Belgian eID cannot be used with Snap or Flatpak software because sandbox confinement blocks the PKCS#11 module; a natively packaged browser is required.
quote: Why is it not possible to use the eID with software in snap and/or Flatpak?

claim: OnlyOffice uses OOXML as its native internal format giving better .docx/.xlsx fidelity, and uses JavaScript macros rather than VBA; LibreOffice converts to OOXML on export.
quote: ONLYOFFICE was deliberately built around the Office Open XML (OOXML) format... LibreOffice does offer limited support for Microsoft VBA macros, while ONLYOFFICE takes a totally different approach, relying on its own JavaScript-based scripting.

claim: OnlyOffice Desktop Editors is the open-source cross-platform office suite with native Linux builds.
quote: ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors: free office suite for document editing and collaboration on Windows, Linux and macOS.

claim: LibreOffice offers only partial VBA support via a compatibility option and a macro converter.
quote: Some simple VBA macros can run in LibreOffice with the Compatibility option, but it not work with all of VBA codes.

claim: Microsoft retired the dedicated Teams desktop client for Linux in December 2022 in favour of the PWA.
quote: Retirement of Teams Desktop App on Linux and New Progressive Web App (PWA)

claim: Microsoft made the Teams PWA generally available for Linux, available only in Edge and Chrome, adding features the retired Electron client lacked.
quote: The PWA experience is available for both Edge and Chrome browsers running on Linux and offers access to more capabilities, including custom backgrounds, gallery view, reactions, the raise-a-hand feature in meetings.

claim: Teams screen sharing on Linux is the recurring failure point, tied to Wayland/PipeWire portal configuration and the browser version.
quote: [Fixed]Screen sharing on Ubuntu is not working (Teams for Web, Teams PWA, Linux)

claim: Independent coverage confirming Thunderbird 145's native Exchange support and its limits.
quote: Thunderbird 145 finally adds 'native' Exchange support

claim: Microsoft begins blocking EWS in Exchange Online on 1 October 2026 with full retirement in April 2027; F1/F3/Kiosk licences were blocked from 1 March 2026. On-premises Exchange is unaffected.
quote: As phased EWS disablement in Exchange Online approaches in October 2026, Microsoft introduced EWSAllowedAppIDs to help administrators prepare in a controlled and predictable way.

claim: Rider is free for non-commercial use (learning, open source, hobby); commercial use still requires a paid licence.
quote: Non-commercial use includes learning, open-source project development, content creation, or hobby development.

claim: WPF and WinForms applications only run on Windows; EnableWindowsTargeting permits building on Linux but not running or designing.
quote: WPF and WinForms applications only run on Windows.

claim: DBeaver and Beekeeper Studio are the leading cross-platform SSMS alternatives running on Windows, macOS and Linux.
quote: The best cross-platform alternatives to SSMS in 2026 are DBeaver and Beekeeper Studio, both of which run on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

claim: The WMI cmdlets were removed in PowerShell 6+, and the CIM cmdlets that replaced them were never ported to non-Windows platforms.
quote: The WMI cmdlets are deprecated and aren't available in PowerShell 6+... There are no plans to port the CIM cmdlets to non-Windows.

claim: Photopea has the best PSD compatibility of the free Photoshop alternatives, preserving layer styles, smart objects and adjustment layers; GIMP and Krita cover photo editing and illustration natively.
quote: Photopea has the best PSD compatibility of any free tool - it reads and preserves layer styles, smart objects, adjustment layers, and text layers.

claim: Canva acquired Affinity in 2024 and moved it to a free unified app in 2025, with native releases for Windows and macOS only.
quote: Affinity was acquired by Canva in 2024 and moved to a freemium model in 2025, with Photo, Designer and Publisher tools now unified into a single free app for Windows and macOS.

claim: An unofficial Affinity v3 AppImage bundles Wine so Canva's Affinity suite runs on Ubuntu without manual Wine setup.
quote: An unofficial Affinity v3 AppImage runs Canva's creative suite on Ubuntu via a simple, self-contained executable without needing to fight with Wine dependencies.

claim: AffinityOnLinux provides community install paths for Affinity via Wine, Bottles, Lutris or Heroic.
quote: A repository that helps users get affinity software working on GNU/Linux

claim: OpenConnect implements Cisco AnyConnect, Palo Alto GlobalProtect, F5 Big-IP and Fortinet FortiGate SSL VPN protocols on Linux.
quote: OpenConnect is an SSL VPN client initially created to support Cisco's AnyConnect SSL VPN and has since been extended to support Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect SSL VPN, F5 Big-IP SSL VPN, and Fortinet Fortigate SSL VPN.

claim: GlobalProtect-openconnect is a Rust GUI/CLI GlobalProtect client for Linux supporting SSO, MFA and YubiKey.
quote: A GlobalProtect VPN client for Linux, written in Rust, based on OpenConnect and Tauri, supports SSO with MFA, Yubikey, etc.

claim: Belgian eID middleware (eid-mw, eid-viewer) ships official packages for Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Mint 21.3/22.3, Fedora 43/44, RHEL 10 plus Rocky/Alma, and openSUSE Leap 16.
quote: After installing the eID-archive package, users install either or both of these: eid-viewer, eid-mw

claim: itsme is activated through a Belgian bank app or with an eID plus card reader when the bank does not offer in-app activation.
quote: You can activate your account with your eID if your bank doesn't offer direct activation, and you will need a card reader for this.

claim: Under Wine, Office 2016 and older work partially; Office 365/2021/2024 do not work reliably because of click-to-run installers, and Outlook/OneDrive/OneNote are broken or absent.
quote: Some components like Onedrive, Outlook and Onenote don't work or with limited features.

claim: WinApps and WinBoat run a managed Windows VM and export individual app windows to the Linux desktop over RemoteApp/RDP, giving far higher compatibility than Wine.
quote: It runs a real copy of Windows inside a managed virtual machine and exports individual Windows program windows to your Linux compositor using Microsoft's RemoteApp/Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

claim: KVM with virt-manager supports real PCI/VFIO passthrough and VirtIO drivers with low overhead, unlike VirtualBox's weaker 3D and passthrough support.
quote: GPU passthrough with virt-manager, QEMU, and KVM

claim: Single-GPU passthrough works without a second card but hands the GPU to the VM, taking the host desktop offline for the duration.
quote: Single-GPU passthrough is possible with QEMU/KVM via virt-manager, requiring no second GPU or remote display streaming.

claim: A Windows 365 Cloud PC is reachable from any HTML5 browser, so no Linux client is needed.
quote: the only requirement is access to an HTML 5 browser, so most modern devices with online access will do the job, whether they run Windows 11 or 10, macOS, Linux, iOS, or Android.

claim: Windows 365 Business runs roughly $28-$56 per user per month after a 20% cut effective 1 May 2026; Enterprise starts near $31 and scales past $120.
quote: Microsoft offers Basic, Standard, and Premium configurations for Windows 365 Business ranging from $28 to $56 per user per month, reflecting a permanent 20% reduction effective May 1, 2026.

claim: Windows 10 support ended 14 October 2025; consumer ESU enrollment is free with settings sync, 1,000 Rewards points, or a one-time $30, and the programme ends 12 October 2027.
quote: You can enroll in ESU any time until the program ends on October 12, 2027... One-time purchase of $30 USD or local currency equivalent plus applicable tax.

claim: Windows 11 24H2 can auto-enable BitLocker even on Home editions; suspend BitLocker and disable Fast Startup before repartitioning, and expect Secure Boot to require signing third-party kernel modules.
quote: Before attempting dual boot installation, confirm BitLocker is suspended or disabled, and disable Windows Fast Startup. Windows 11 24H2 may enable BitLocker automatically on fresh installs, even on Home editions.

claim: A shared EFI System Partition can be damaged by hibernating or Fast-Startup-shutting-down one OS then booting the other; install Windows first and reuse but never reformat the ESP.
quote: If you share one EFI system partition between Windows and Linux, then the EFI system partition may be damaged if you hibernate (or shutdown with Fast Startup enabled) Windows and then start Linux, or hibernate Linux and then start Windows.

claim: The EFI System Partition should be at least 260 MiB to guarantee correct FAT32 formatting and avoid firmware compatibility issues.
quote: The UEFI System Partition should be at least 260 MiB (273 MB) to ensure its properly formatted with FAT32 so that you avoid UEFI implementation compatibility issues.

claim: Windows reads the hardware clock as local time while Linux writes UTC, causing a recurring clock skew; fix by setting Linux to keep local time in the RTC or Windows to UTC.
quote: Windows assumes local time, while Linux assumes UTC time, causing time discrepancies in dual boot situations.

claim: The in-kernel ntfs3 driver has caused freezes and disk corruption; ntfs-3g is slower but the stable choice.
quote: Blacklist ntfs3 and use ntfs-3g for slower but stable experience

claim: exFAT has native read-write support in the Linux kernel and on macOS, making it the practical shared-partition format, but it carries no POSIX permissions or extended attributes.
quote: Microsoft opened up the exFAT specification in 2019, and now Linux has native read-write support in the kernel, with macOS also offering native read-write support.

claim: Dropbox on Linux supports only unencrypted ext4 for the sync folder because it relies on extended attributes; ext4 inside a LUKS volume is still fine, but ext4's own file-based encryption is not.
quote: Dropbox relies on extended attributes (X-attrs) to identify files in the Dropbox folder and keep them in sync... they would keep supporting only the most common file systems that support X-attrs.

claim: The Dropbox Linux client requires Ubuntu 18.04+/Fedora 28+, GTK/GDK 2.24+, libappindicator, and a desktop environment that supports AppIndicator.
quote: Ubuntu 64-bit: 18.04 or later; Fedora 64-bit: 28 or later; GTK 2.24 or later; GDK 2.24 or later; Glib 2.40 or later; Libappindicator 12.10 or later

claim: Container startup is ~0.3s native vs ~1.2s on WSL2 and container filesystem operations are 3-5x faster natively; WSL2 falls short for kernel work and USB/GPU passthrough.
quote: Container startup is 0.3s on Linux vs 1.2s on Windows (WSL2), and file system operations inside containers are 3-5x faster on Linux.

claim: WSL2 networking defaults to NAT and is isolated from the host network stack, whereas native Linux offers bridged and host-only configurations.
quote: by default, WSL2 networks are isolated from the host network, which can be a drawback for applications requiring direct access to the host's network stack or specific IP configurations.
